original_card.question: Does one explicit extension of the connector alphabet offer a favorable completed budget?
methods: Construct and charge a legal extra operation on a minimal instance.
Prove a target-specific bound after adding one specified operation family.
original_card.acceptance_gate: State which fixed-alphabet premise changes and charge its implementation; do not declare it free.

first_step.inspect: Reproduce the 945-pairing control, then read Exact interface to list the allowed calls.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Add exactly one legally priced operation and test a tiny dirty-input instance before enumerating larger cases.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A new legal connector operation could change recursive interface cost; a larger census in the same alphabet is a separate side result.
allowed_variations: Choose one additional operation and a small source count for its first counterexample.
scope_change_triggers: Keeping the alphabet and only increasing the source count; record this as a changed assignment.

actual_scope: Six-source universal source path in the connector alphabet extended by exactly the pair-source DUO family (charged weight-2 steps, sources read-only): exact Pareto question for (k calls, W source adds) against the singleton value f(6)=16, with a bounded seeded search, exact lower bounds and exact exclusions; plus a counting closure of the five-source weight-at-most-3 question (side result, labelled).
scope_change_reason: The card's own variation domain (one added operation, small source count, first counterexample) is saturated: merged research/duo-toggle-connector owns the DUO family at n=3 and n=5 with n=4 as a side row, and the concurrent open PR https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2056 restates the five-source result (claimed 2026-10-14 17:42 UTC in Discussion 1166). The scope-change trigger of the card says that keeping an alphabet and increasing the source count is a changed assignment; the six-source count is exactly research/duo-toggle-connector's own open question 2, recorded there as search-blocked, so the change continues the card's one-operation question at its first unsaturated boundary. The side result keeps the card's operation-variation shape (a charged three-source call) and closes open question 3 of the same predecessor.
bottleneck_link: Connector call cost enters the recursive interface through complete-call pricing: the DUO family lowers the six-source all-63-row batch from 142 to 140 root queries at unchanged 142 source adds (saving exactly two per-call overheads o). No physical supplier instance of this connector interface exists; that predecessor limitation is unchanged and no kappa is claimed.
stop_rule: Seeded search capped at about two minutes total across (k, n_duos) cells; exact controls and censuses must pass; stop after one found universal word or the cap; no second pivot.
evidence: Explicit six-source DUO universal word of k=14 calls / W=16 adds (two weight-2 steps), all 64 masks covered, replayed exactly by a code-disjoint checker (dual coverage test); Pareto-improves singleton (16,16) since k=14 < 16 with W=16 equal; batch 140 queries at 142 adds vs singleton 142/142. Exact exclusions: (12,12) by the complete 10,395-word all-unit k=12 census (max 49/64, reproducing research/universal-connector-six-source); (14,14) all-unit by its cited census (max 59/64); W<k impossible; (12,14) best 53/64, (12,16) best 58/64, (13,14) best 56/64, (13,16) best 63/64 remain open (scoped search failures, not exclusions). Side lemma: at five sources W=10, k=10 forces all-unit words (max 31/32, complete 945-word census), so no charged three-source call lowers W below 12 at k=10 and the five-source Pareto (10,12) is optimal for the whole weight-at-most-3 alphabet. Command: python3 -B research/connector-six-source-duo/verify.py -> PASS_CONNECTOR_SIX_DUO witness=(14,16) n5max=31 k12max=49 mutations=4.
